_readme: Linux root filesystem images drac-Xterm can download, keyed by Android ABI.
The app reads Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS first and only shows the entries under a
matching key. arm64-v8a is the main ABI; phones use it.
Adding another ABI here means building its proot/busybox binaries first, or the
download succeeds and nothing in it can run.
The x86_64 section is for emulator/WayDroid/ChromeOS and is still marked as
testing. Its Debian image is the images.linuxcontainers.org build 20260919_05:24,
mirrored because that host keeps dated builds for only about three days: the
20260913_05:24 build pinned while 1.0.5 was in development answered 404 before
1.0.5 shipped. The mirror release also carries that build's original SHA256SUMS
and its GPG signature (key E7FB0CAEC8173D669066514CBAEFF88C22F6E216, "LXC
pre-built images"), so the digest can be traced upstream after the rotation.
Every entry carries a sha256. RootfsDownloader refuses to hand an archive to
the extractor unless the digest of the completed file matches exactly. An
entry without a valid 64-hex digest is dropped when this file is parsed.
All five images come from one place now: the release assets of
github.com/ExsoKamabay/rootless, a mirror this project controls. For the four
arm64 images the bytes and the digests are the same as before; the host is what
changed. That repository also publishes SHA256SUMS on its main branch, and that
is the file scripts/verify-rootfs-urls.sh reads to check the pins below.
Why each source moved:
* The three Kali images were served by kali.download, which is still healthy.
Its SHA256SUMS for kali-2026.2 lists exactly the three digests pinned below,
so each one can still be re-derived from the Kali project itself.
* The Debian image has outlived two hosts. easycli.sh carried it until its
operator disabled hosting for good; the URL answered 302 -> / with a 43-byte
notice, and the SHA-256 pin correctly refused to install it.
images.linuxcontainers.org replaced it and published a signed SHA256SUMS, but
that server keeps only about three days of dated builds. The 20260904_05:24
URL shipped in 1.0.1 through 1.0.3 answers 404 today, exactly as the previous
version of this note warned it would.
The entry below is the proot-distro build this project pinned in 1.0.0
(9bd3b19f...), served from the mirror. Its digest can no longer be re-derived
from an outside authority, because the host that published it is gone; what
stands behind it is the pin this project has carried since its first release.
Re-pointing an entry at another host is safe while the digest stays the same.
The bytes are what gets verified here, not the address they arrived from.
